annotations.title: Change an indicator's settings on my open Vela chart

description: Changes settings of one indicator on the chart the signed-in member has open right now in Vela, as its settings dialog would: a length, a source, a mode, a toggle, a colour. Name the indicator by the id vela_read_chart gives it and each setting by the name vela_get_indicator_settings lists; read the settings first rather than guessing names. Use it when the member asks to tune an indicator on their chart ("set the RSI length to 21", "turn off the labels"). Vela checks every value against what the indicator declares before anything changes: a setting it does not have, or a value it does not allow, changes nothing and the result says why and lists the settings. The indicator re-runs with the new values in front of the member, who is told an assistant changed their chart; the script itself is not edited (to change what an indicator does, quant_generate_pine_script). Returns each setting changed, from what to what, and what the chart shows afterwards. With the member's Vela tab on screen it happens in front of them within seconds. When it is not (they are in another tab), the change is queued and applied the moment they look at Vela again, within 10 minutes: the result then says queued, so tell them to open Vela. Requires signing in with a LuxAlgo account (OAuth).

context.description: Explain in 15-25 words, in third person, why this tool is called and how it supports the user's goal. For analytics only. You MUST describe only the abstract purpose of the tool call. NEVER include, repeat, paraphrase, or infer personal, sensitive, or identifying information from the user request or tool results, including names, emails, phone numbers, IPs, IDs, or credentials. You MUST generalize specific entities into roles such as "a user", "the customer", or "an account". Example: "Retrieving a customer's recent orders to investigate a billing issue and help support determine the appropriate resolution."

id.description: The indicator, by the id vela_read_chart gives it, e.g. "i_0k3v9qa1x7m2pd".

settings.description: The settings to change; the rest keep their values.

name.description: The setting's name as vela_get_indicator_settings lists it.

value.description: The new value: a number, true or false, or text (one of the choices, a hex colour like #2962ff).

slot.description: One chart of a multi-chart layout, by position (0 is the top-left, in reading order). Leave it out for the chart the member is working on.
